articleTitle: Wideband saline-water antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Basic monopole antennas are becoming less suitable for wireless communications because most applications demand multi-band operation. Dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) can be made with a wide range of materials and allow many excitation methods. We are investigating liquid dielectrics as DRAs at frequencies between 1-4 GHz. In this paper we report a variable height liquid antenna. We used pure water which has good dielectric properties for frequencies up to 2 GHZ salt (NaCl salinity S<4ppt) was added to reduce the dielectric response of water at high frequencies (<2 GHz). As a development to where the match was tuned by varying the length of the antenna; the resonant frequency of the proposed antenna is now changed by varying the liquid column height.

articleTitle: Utilisation and tuning of the chassis modes of a handheld terminal for the design of multiband radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: The essential role of the resonant modes of the surface current density distribution on the chassis of a small size handheld terminal for its multiband radiation properties is discussed. An easy-to-implement practical approach for chassis mode analysis by post-processing of output data from standard CEM software packages is presented. The purposeful utilization and the tuning of chassis modes for the design of multiband radiation characteristics on generic bar-type and folder-type geometries are demonstrated and numerical results are given for several canonical examples.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental investigation of adaptive antenna impedance matching for multiband mobile phone applications
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Adaptive impedance matching is an attractive option to extend the operational bandwidth of a mobile phone antenna system beyond the limits set by available antenna and device volume and, moreover, to adapt to varying near field environment. Theoretical and experimental results on the attainable improvement in power transfer and on compliance with the tough linearity requirements of mobile phone standards, questions which are central to the assessment of feasibility in product applications are reported.

articleTitle: Tunable C-band frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A novel tunable frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented that can simultaneously block both polarisations, vertical and horizontal. The filter, which consists of convoluted dipole elements, can be tuned over a wide frequency range within the C-band frequency spectrum, at around 5.2 GHz. Its tunability is achieved by employing lumped element varactor diodes.

articleTitle: Characterisation of printed UWB antennas for on-body communications
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Low-profile, compact and easily integrated body worn antennas are the essence of efficient, reliable and user-friendly body-centric networks. The paper presents different planar printed ultra wideband (UWB) antennas and their applications as part of on-body communication systems. Both frequency and time domain characteristics of the proposed antennas are investigated and analysed. The paper emphasises the importance of chosen frequency band on propagation channels behaviour. On-body propagation characterisation is experimentally investigated to highlight antennas and human body effects on radio channels and consequently on the wireless body-centric network performance.

articleTitle: Progress of multi-band antenna technology in mobile phone industry
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Summary form only given. In the 1990's, the mobile phone industry experienced a dramatic development. The first stage was from analog standard to digital standard development, for example, analog standard such as AMPS (advanced mobile phone system), NMT (Nordic mobile telephone) and ETACS; digital standard such as GSM, D-AMPS and CDMA. The second stage was from single band to multi-band due to the strong capacity requirements. DCS 1800 and PCS 1900 were introduced in the middle of 1990's. Ying first proposed a dual band non-uniform helical antenna which became a popular antenna for dual band mobile phones. In the same time, P. Haapala proposed a dual band mono-helix antenna while G. Hayes proposed a meander type dual band antenna. In 1997, Ying proposed a branch multi-band antenna which has been applied into several Ericsson mobile phones. Andersson proposed a broad band shark fin antenna later. In 1998, an internal antenna was introduced to the mobile phone, which caused a lot of market interest. We started some research work in this area and soon Ying proposed an internal printed spiral antenna and a dual band printed antenna. Later in the same year, a dual band internal antenna for a mobile phone was developed. The antenna concept is based on a branched PIFA antenna. Today, many of dual band mobile handsets use this kind antenna concept. To meet the global system requirement, some so-called penta band antenna concepts are proposed. The capacitive feeding and high dielectric loading are introduced in the new concept. The multi-band technique is still a hot topic in the mobile terminal application.

articleTitle: Quad-band handset antenna operation for GSM900/DCS1800/PCS1900/UMTS
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A novel compact quadband internal planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) for handsets covering the bands GSM-900, DCS-1800, PCS-1900 and UMTS is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a planar antenna element suspended parallel above the dielectric of a single sided PCB. By etching a section of the conducting ground plane below the radiating element, the antenna gains the merits of a planar monopole and consequently a wider bandwidth. The antenna occupies a total volume of 38 mm /spl times/ 25 mm /spl times/ 6 mm and is well suited as internal antenna due to its low profile, small size, wide bandwidth and multi-band behavior. The antenna structure, simulation and measurements of return losses, radiation patterns and specific absorption rate (SAR) are also discussed.

articleTitle: Integration of electrically small UWB antennas for body-worn sensor applications
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: In this paper we compare characteristics of electrically small UWB monopole and slot antennas, when they operate as stand-alone radiators, and after integration into body-worn sensors. A simplified model of wearable sensors was used a solid metal sheet of about 9 cm/sup 2/. Results show that the integration of antennas significantly changes the return loss and radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Planar PIFA telematics antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: This paper describes printed planar versions of the PIFA antenna for multi-band telematics applications on vehicles. The antennas are variations on the planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) principle and may be customized for different mounting positions such as bumpers, window and roof mount. The printed antennas are small, have a VSWR specification of 2 or better and are designed for low cost production. Each antenna was designed for tri-band mobile telephone band coverage from 890 MHz to 2100 MHz. On-vehicle tests are described for the antennas located on glass and integrated into the bumper on a vehicle.

articleTitle: Wideband dipoles on electromagnetic bandgap ground planes
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: In this paper the broadband diamond dipole antenna performance above an electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure composed of an array of square metallic patches without any via over a PEC backed dielectric substrate is investigated. A bandwidth of 2.5:1, 4.9 GHz to 12.2 GHz is achieved for S/sub 11/; however the radiation pattern degrades above 7 GHz. The gain of the antenna is more than 6 dB over the 3.8 to 6.8 GHz range.

articleTitle: Elliptical multiple ring monopole antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: The effects of the ellipticity ratio and the thickness of the rings on the multiple ring monopole antennas are presented. Several multiple ring monopole antennas with different ellipticity ratios and thickness of the rings are designed, fabricated and measured. The results show that the resonance bandwidths can be controlled by the ellipticity ratio and changing the thickness of the rings causes a frequency shift at the fourth band but it does not have a significant effect on the lower bands.

articleTitle: Multiband MIMO antenna arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: This paper considers the implementation of multiple element antenna arrays for MIMO wireless systems for use with multiple wireless standards operating at different frequencies. The capacity of such systems for a realistic channel model is considered, and it is shown that it is not generally worthwhile to reduce element spacing below 0.4 wavelengths, and proposes an array topology using a mixture of multi-band and single band elements to maximise the benefit of MIMO while minimising the hardware requirements. Some examples of multi-band elements are given.

articleTitle: Optimizing the design examples of wide-band antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: The examples described in this paper illustrate the application of computational electromagnetics in the design of realistic multi- and wideband antennas. With the model generation, solver, optimization and post processing utilities of modern software tools, and the capabilities of today's desktop computers, the CONCERTO rf design process can be very rapid. The number of build and test iterations can be dramatically reduced, with consequent reduction in cost and time scale. Relevant antenna design examples are given to illustrate its capability and utility.

articleTitle: Multi-band material loaded low-SAR antenna for mobile handsets
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Previous studies have shown that monopoles loaded with material of equal permittivity and permeability values give increased bandwidth and radiation efficiency for a given size reduction. Positioning the monopole orthogonally to the head directs pattern nulls towards the head, which leads to low specific absorption rates (SAR). Simulated results of the material loaded monopole showed dual-mode behaviour. In this paper, the simple monopole is translated into a compact antenna design suitable for mobile handsets. Metallic strips are printed on the material block to increase the number of modes and realise a small, quad-band, low-SAR handset antenna.

articleTitle: Slot-inserted semi-circular disc antenna for wideband communications
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: This paper proposes a slot-inserted semi-circular disc (SCD) antenna fed by a microstrip for wideband applications. The antenna gives a bandwidth of 3.9-8.9 GHz for S/sub 11/ < -10 dB with a very compact size. Rectangular and circular slots have been studied for the bandwidth improvement. Parametric study has been carried out to optimize the performance. The simulated results are in good agreement with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Now class of multi-band and ultra-wideband printed dipole antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)

articleTitle: Wideband microstrip patch radiators for a future synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: There is a constant drive to achieve better performance from antennas designed to work as part of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The beam steering requirements remain sensibly unaltered but greater fractional bandwidth becomes essential and dual-linear polarization is likely to become a desirable feature. Antennas that can meet these anticipated future needs are planar phased arrays and potential designs have been reported in the open literature. This paper describes some of the continuing work performed at EADS Astrium Ltd to investigate antennas that meet the technical needs of a future SAR.

articleTitle: Broadband matched-to-air microstrip antennas (MAMA)
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: The present paper proposes a new reformulation of microstrip antenna design based on multisection Chebsyshev impedance matching transformers. The new proposed design procedure aims to match the feedline impedance to that of the air using the antenna to be designed. A sample design example is presented. Simulation results using Fidelity and IE3D softwares show that the proposed procedure is a promising method for designing microstrip broadband antennas.

articleTitle: Modelling of miniaturised multiband 3D slot loop antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A novel miniaturised multiband 3D slot loop antenna is proposed as a built-in terminal antenna with multiple bands of individual broad bandwidth. The antenna is constructed three-dimensionally by printing a rectangular slot loop antenna with a narrow outer conductor on the surface of a substrate box. The chip-formed antenna is then mounted on the top edge of the ground plane of the PCB. Simulation results of the proposed antenna with dimensions of 20 mm /spl times/ 24 mm /spl times/ 1.12 mm on a substrate box of dielectric constant /spl epsi//sub r/ = 6 show the -6 dB bandwidths of 1.78 GHz (1.37 - 3.15 GHz) in the first band and 0.82 GHz (3.74 - 4.56 GHz) in the second band. Compared with the corresponding flat slot loop antenna, the 3D slot loop antenna not only reduces the size by a factor of 2, but also provides wider bandwidth in both bands. Furthermore, the proposed 3D slot loop has a balanced structure which is insensitive to the perturbation of the ground plane. The antenna can be designed for specific applications with the adjustment of appropriate dimensions.

articleTitle: Dual frequency microstrip antenna with V slot
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A dual-frequency (C- and X- band) microstrip antenna is proposed and the simulation results of its performance are reported. The antenna unit can be incorporated into arrays, and offer the possibility of a compact, light-weight and cost effective antenna array design for various applications such as television broadcasting, wireless communications and radar systems.

articleTitle: Tunable absorber based on electromagnetic band gap surface and a lossy resistance sheet
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A novel tunable absorber is presented in which a resistive sheet of indium tin oxide (ITO) is placed on top of an electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) surface. The untuned absorber is effective over a narrow frequency band. However, by virtue of tunability it can operate over other frequency bands. Tunability is achieved by employing varactor diodes on the EBG surface.

articleTitle: Wideband random phased arrays: theory and design
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Wideband antennas may be used to decrease the number of antennas needed on platforms that require operation over a large instantaneous frequency band. Some typical examples of wideband antennas include TEM horns and Vivaldi tapered slot antennas. Although these antennas offer wideband operation, they are often not suitable for certain applications due to large thickness, weight, and complicated feed networks. On the other hand, typical planar phased arrays have limited frequency bandwidth and scan angles. There is a need to mitigate this issue by using a smaller random array as a subarray, resulting in a hybrid array whose pattern has some of the characteristics of both periodic and aperiodic arrays. One possible alternative to these kinds of antennas is the wideband random phased array. In addition to the design of the array topology, another challenge is to develop a low profile, electrically large element that maintains a broadside radiation pattern over the operating band. In this paper, the authors developed a wideband element design of a canted, tapered sector antenna that delivers consistent broadside performance over a 2.8:1 frequency band. The authors conclude with a brief discussion of future work in this area.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna for 802.1 a wlan applications
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)

articleTitle: Input and far-field responses of compact UWB antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: With the desire for ever-increasing data-rates, coupled with the interest in techniques that offer interference mitigation, much research has focused upon ultra wide-band (UWB) systems that can theoretically realise such benefits. In practice, any UWB system will require an antenna to connect it (the radio) to free-space. Through examples of practical measurements from two different UWB antennas, this paper will discuss the characteristics that must be considered when assessing UWB antennas.

articleTitle: Frequency domain finite element modeling of 2d parallel-plate waveguide antenna array
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)

articleTitle: Switchable dual circularly polarised ultra wideband antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A circularly polarised antenna capable of switching between left and right polarisation is presented. The antenna operates over a 2 to 18 GHz bandwidth. The antenna has an integrated switch, RF limiter and DC control circuitry.

articleTitle: Higher order modes in a wideband ringloaded horn
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: A ringloaded horn has been designed and manufactured to cover a bandwidth of 8 to 18 GHz. The requirements were a peak gain of more than 15 dBi and a coaxial output. These requirements led to a design in which a ringloaded horn was followed by a dual ridged waveguide section with a coaxial output.

articleTitle: Study on the transmission of RF signals on the human body
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of the human body on the RF transmission is investigated by using a finite difference time-domain method. A wearable PIFA operating at ISM-2.4 GHz is used in the analysis. The antennas are placed on different parts of the body including the head, waist, shoulder, and heart. The potential of using the human body as a means of transmitting RF signals is discussed.

articleTitle: The benefits of circuit and antenna co-simulation for optimising wideband structures
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: One of the main challenges in designing wideband antennas that are both small and high performance, is how this performance is affected when the antenna is integrated into the rest of the system. This paper details how dynamically co-simulating the antenna with the critical parts of the system, allows the designer to jointly optimise the overall solution. An example of an UWB antenna co-simulated with a matching circuit is presented, and this paper shows how it is possible to trade-off antenna size against the matching circuit whilst still maintaining a good overall performance.

articleTitle: Small antennas for personal communications devices
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: The necessity of multi-standard mobile communications devices represents a challenge for antenna designers, as they have to implement integrated multiband elements within a volume which is rapidly shrinking. This paper shows some examples of multiband antenna solutions for this kind of applications.

articleTitle: Contents
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)

articleTitle: Printed triband terminal antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: This paper presents a printed triple-band multibranch monopole for use in modern wireless systems. The antenna is designed to operate in three bands which cover virtually all wireless channels. Parameters of the antenna geometry are varied and the effects of these variations on the impedance bandwidth are shown.

articleTitle: Wideband printed Fresnel reflector antenna in W-band
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: Millimeter wave radar becomes has been increasingly used in the defense sector and civil applications like automotive cruise control or helicopter crash avoidance. Parallel to this development, antennas have to support an increasing number of functions that can be provided by the augmentation of their bandwidth or multiband operating modes. Although wideband and multiband single printed antennas are now more developed, millimeter wave wideband arrays remain limited because of their complexity and metallic losses. In this paper, The authors present a printed millimeter wave reflector using circular patches centered at 94 GHz suitable for radar applications whose elements and primary source have been designed to achieve about 9 % bandwidth in terms of reflection coefficient and gain.

articleTitle: The synthesis of wideband arrays using nature-based design concepts
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: In order to meet the growing demands of modern radar and communication systems, engineers often turn to nature for their inspiration. Genetic algorithms (GA), optimization techniques based on the Darwinian notion of survival of the fittest, have recently been applied to find solutions to these complex design problems. In addition, complicated geometries of many natural objects such as trees, ferns, coastlines, and vascular systems could be described simply with the advent of fractal geometry. Fractal geometry has also been applied to create a class of antenna arrays, called fractal-random arrays, which combine the physical and electrical properties of periodic and random arrays into one design. In previous research, The authors introduced a specialized subset of fractal-random arrays, that is now called polyfractal arrays, which are particularly adept in genetic algorithm optimization. In addition, the authors introduced a new type of nature-based design process which applies a robust genetic algorithm technique to evolve optimal polyfractal array layouts. In this paper, the authors consider several nature-based design examples, which illustrate that optimized fractal-random arrays can possess extremely large bandwidths.

articleTitle: Small terminal antennas within the ACE Network of Excellence
publicationTitle: IEE Wideband and Multi-band Antennas and Arrays 2005 (Ref. No. 2005/11059)
abstract: This paper deals with the work on technologies for small terminal antennas carried out within the ACE Network of Excellence. The aim is to ascertain the state of the art in this field, and identify the future trends in antenna design for personal communications devices.
